question.problem: Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on the set $A=\{0,1,2,…,9\},$ defined by $a∼b$ if $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi b}{2}).$ How many distinct equivalence classes does $∼$ partition $A$ into?
question.worked_solution:
The equivalence classes of $∼$ partition $A,$ meaning that any element $a\in A$ belongs to exactly one distinct equivalence class.

So, we compute equivalence classes until all the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class.

$$
\begin{aligned}[0] & =\{a\in A∣a∼0\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 0}{2})\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=1\} \\  & =\{0,4,8\} \\  \\ [1] & =\{a\in A∣a∼1\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 1}{2})\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=0\} \\  & =\{1,3,5,7,9\} \\  \\ [2] & =\{a\in A∣a∼2\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 2}{2})\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )\} \\  & =\{a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi a}{2})=-1\} \\  & =\{2,6\}\end{aligned}
$$

All of the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class, so we are done.

We have $3$ distinct equivalence classes:

$$
[0]=\{0,4,8\},\,[1]=\{1,3,5,7,9\},\,[2]=\{2,6\}.
$$
